did.abstract: The Hesung Chun Koh Family Papers and East Rock Institute Records document the professional and personal activities of various Koh family members, including Dr. Hesung Chun Koh, Dr. Kwang Lim Koh, and Harold Hongju Koh. The East Rock Institute (ERI) records contain the business, research, and educational activites of the organization. The collection is comprised of correspondence, course materials, writings, research notes, interviews, and publications created by, or related to, the Koh family and the East Rock Institute. Research strengths of the collection are the history of Korean and Korean-American studies in the United States and cross-cultural scholarship between Korea and the United States.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Hesung Chun Koh Family Papers and East Rock Institute Records document the professional and personal activities of various Koh family members, including Dr. Hesung Chun Koh, Dr. Kwang Lim Koh, and Harold Hongju Koh. The East Rock Institute (ERI) records contain the business, research, and educational activites of the organization. The collection is comprised of correspondence, course materials, writings, research notes, interviews, and publications created by, or related to, the Koh family and the East Rock Institute. Research strengths of the collection are the history of Korean and Korean-American studies in the United States and cross-cultural scholarship between Korea and the United States.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Hesung Chun (전혜성) was born on July 3, 1929 in Seoul, Korea under Japanese occupation. She attended Ewha Women's University before coming to the United States as an exchange student in 1948. She earned a BA in economics and sociology from Dickinson College before continuing her education at Boston University where she earned an MA and subsequent PhD in sociology and anthropology. She married Kwang Lim Koh in 1951.

Kwang Lim Koh (고광림) was born on October 20, 1920 on Jeju island during the occupation of Korea by Japan. He studied law at what became Seoul National University before immigrating to the United States in 1949. He earned several advanced degrees: MA and PhD in political science from Rutgers University; Master of Laws and Doctorate of Juridicial Science from Harvard Law School; and a Bachelor of Laws in Common Law from Boston College.

Together, Hesung Chun Koh and Kwang Lim Koh started the Korea Institute in Boston, the first non-profit cultural organization dedicated to Korean and Korean-American culture and history, and the predecessor of the East Rock Institute. From 1960-1961 Kwang Lim Koh was appointed Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary to the Korea Mission to the United Nations, and the family moved to Washington, D.C. Afterwards, the Koh family moved to New Haven, Connecticut, where Kwang Lim Koh taught courses at the Yale Law School before becoming the Director of the Center for International and Area Studies at Central Connecticul State University.

Hesung Chun Koh joined the research staff of the Human Relations Area Files at Yale University, where she worked from 1961-1988 and eventually became Director of East Asian Area Research. Along with her spouse, she co-taught a seminar on East Asian Law and Society at the Yale Law School from 1963-1966 and served on the faculty of the Yale Department of Sociology from 1961-1985. Over the years, Hesung Chun Koh has conducted research on a variety of topics related to Korean and Korean-American life and culture.

The East Rock Institute, established in 1985, continues the work of the Korea Institute by preserving and promoting the heritage of Korean culture and identity by providing intercultural experiences and research. It was early pioneer in the development of educational, scholarly, and culture programs including: an annual conference of Korean and Korean Americans (1970-2009); curriculum development for courses and workshops on Korean culture and history (2005-2019); and the Korean and Korean American Studies Bulletin (1984-2009).
Other members of the Koh family represented in the collection include Carolyn Kyongshin Koh Choo; Howard Kyongju, Edward Tongju, Harold Hongju, Jean Kyongun Koh Peters, and Richard Jongju.
Kwang Lim Koh died on September 17, 1989.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The series details the history, development, and activites of the East Rock Institute, including courses taught in Korean and Korean-American studies, the creation of cultural information systems, and issues of the Korean and Korean-American Bulletin . Materials include course syllabi and reading lists, publications, correspondence, reports, and research notes.
